findings.claim: The decision solves a narrower problem than the operator asked for by reducing “ALL the features” of UAR/AG-UI/A2UI to displayable conversation parts.
findings.evidence: Original intent requires “AG-UI as the protocol with full support for A2UI and its agent definitions standards, content management algorithm selection, skill selection algorithms, and ALL the features it provides”; the decision only maps streams to `UIMessageChunk`, A2UI surfaces/actions, telemetry, and two UAR-side event fixes, with no decision for agent definitions standards, content management algorithm selection, or skill selection algorithms.
findings.suggested_fix: Add explicit decisions for each named UAR feature in the intent, or state which features are intentionally out of scope and obtain an operator decision accepting that reduced scope.

findings.claim: The falsifier is not operational because it gives no thresholds, test fixtures, measurement method, or timeframe for deciding failure.
findings.evidence: The falsifier uses subjective or undefined triggers: “A realistic UAR run loses information the user needs,” “visible lag,” “unbounded message growth,” “cannot coexist,” and “offers a maintained client,” none of which specify what run, what user-needed information, what lag threshold, what growth bound, what dependency conflict criteria, or by when the ecosystem research must be complete.
findings.suggested_fix: Define executable falsification checks, e.g. named UAR trace fixtures must round-trip with ordered events and attributed reasoning; snapshot re-emission must stay under a specified latency and persistence-size budget for a streaming-table fixture; package install/build must pass in the-boss repo without duplicate React; ecosystem research must be completed before implementation starts.

findings.claim: Two load-bearing assumptions are cheaply checkable now but are left unverified before committing to the architecture.
findings.evidence: The assumptions say “Applying JSON-Patches in the main process and re-emitting whole snapshots is cheap enough” and “`@prometheus-ags/a2ui-uar` can be built and consumed by the-boss despite version differences,” while the falsifier admits these could fail via “visible lag,” “unbounded message growth,” “duplicate React,” “style leakage,” or “dependency conflicts.”
findings.suggested_fix: Require a spike before commitment: replay high-frequency A2UI patch fixtures through the adapter and attempt to install/build/render `@prometheus-ags/a2ui-uar` inside the-boss with its actual dependency graph and Tailwind setup.

findings.claim: The decision depends on UAR changes without establishing ownership, release timing, or fallback behavior if those changes do not ship.
findings.evidence: The decision includes “UAR-side fixes: emit `TEXT_MESSAGE_START/END` on the runs stream; add an error flag and tool name to `TOOL_CALL_RESULT`,” but the packet contains no prior decision, constraint, or plan showing the-boss phase can change UAR or consume a released UAR version containing those fixes.
findings.suggested_fix: Split this into an explicit dependency decision: identify the UAR version/release that must contain these fixes, who owns it, what blocks implementation, and what degraded behavior the-boss uses if the fixes are absent.

findings.claim: The decision defers required alternative analysis until after the decision instead of performing it before choosing the adapter approach.
findings.evidence: Original intent says to “use deep research and adversarial review to determine the best course”; the falsifier says the decision is wrong if “The AG-UI ecosystem (research) offers a maintained client or React renderer for A2UI v0.9,” which means the existence of a better maintained alternative has not been settled before deciding.
findings.suggested_fix: Complete and attach the AG-UI/A2UI ecosystem research before committing, including named alternatives, maintenance status, compatibility with persistence/multi-runtime requirements, and why each was rejected.

findings.claim: The persistence assumption may discard information needed to satisfy replay, audit, debugging, and continuation semantics.
findings.evidence: The assumption says “Persisting the final surface snapshot (not the patch history) is enough to re-render a past conversation,” while the decision also routes user actions through continuation runs and shows telemetry such as “memory recall/mutation, guardrail and sycophancy flags, budget, context usage, sub-agents”; final visual state alone cannot reconstruct how a surface reached that state or what action/patch sequence caused a continuation.
findings.suggested_fix: Define exactly which replay/audit/debug guarantees are required, then decide whether to persist patch history, action events, or a compact event log in addition to the final snapshot.
